office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican Rep. Chris Corry, the House Republican Deputy Minority Leader, faces Democrat Jack McEntire, a Selah sculptor making his third run for a 15th District House seat. Corry has a long voting record against new taxes and the Climate Commitment Act; McEntire's platform centers on universal health care and need-based access to education.

candidates.summary: Four-term State Representative and House Republican Deputy Minority Leader who campaigns on limited government, lower taxes and parental rights.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S6][S7][S8]
Says an income tax should require a constitutional amendment and a vote of the people [S4]
Voted for 2023 middle-housing legalization and against the 2025 rent-increase cap [S10][S11]
Voted against the Climate Commitment Act (2021) and ESHB 1296 (2025) [S9][S12]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346, EHB 2081 and ESSB 5814, and issued repeated statements opposing the income tax and calling for lower tax burdens.

spending.basis: Repeatedly argues the operating budget has doubled in a decade and the state should manage existing revenue before asking for more.

housing.basis: Voted for middle-housing legalization (supply) and against the 2025 cap on residential rent increases.

safety.basis: Voted against the 2021 police-tactics and use-of-force bills; criticizes the Legislature for not holding repeat offenders accountable.

climate.basis: Voted against the Climate Commitment Act in 2021; no campaign statement on climate.

experience.basis: In the House since 2019 and now Deputy Minority Leader, facing a challenger with no government-office record.

social.basis: Voted against ESHB 1469 on access to reproductive and gender-affirming care; lists Life Choices of Yakima among his community service.

parental-rights.basis: Campaigns on parental rights, voted against ESHB 1296 twice, and criticized the Legislature for not acting on the parental-rights initiative.

immigration.basis: Voted against the 2019 Keep Washington Working Act limiting state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement; one vote, no statement.

candidates.summary: Selah sculptor and Yakima County Democrats vice-chair, in his third run for a 15th District House seat, campaigning on universal health care and need-based access to education.
highlights: Says college or vocational education should be based on ability and need, not money [S1]
Called climate change an existential threat in 2020 [S2]
Argues voters have seen "the same faces and ideas" for years [S1]

healthcare.basis: Calls for universal health care and says Washington could provide it, criticizing job-based coverage.

spending.basis: Calls investment the way to transform the region and backs universal education and youth skills programs.

climate.basis: Called climate change an existential threat and urged listening to science (2020); no specific policy stated.

experience.basis: No government-office record; argues voters have seen the same faces and ideas for years.
